title: nixos/phpfpm: escape string values in settings/phpEnv per parse_ini_file rules
test_wiring: nixos/tests/all-tests.nix (head 03ac107a963d2c7910be4443cdd6ed399c5d4c92): `php = import ./php/default.nix { inherit runTest; php = pkgs.php; }` (line ~1339), and nixos/tests/php/default.nix (fetched at head) confirms: `fpm = runTest { imports = [ ./fpm.nix ]; _module.args.php = php'; };` -- fpm.nix is wired.
watch_selection_basis: PR diff (`gh pr diff 516530`) touches nixos/modules/services/web-servers/phpfpm/default.nix inside the `toStr` helper function (a private let-binding used to serialize option *values* into php.ini syntax -- adds a new `isString value` branch with escaping logic), and nixos/tests/php/fpm.nix (adds phpEnv test fixtures + assertions). The touched module lines are NOT inside any mkOption/mkEnableOption/mkRenamedOptionModule/etc. declaration -- toStr is a plain helper function used later when rendering `settings`/`phpEnv` values, confirmed by inspecting the full option declarations (lines 187-260 at head): `settings`, `extraConfig`, `phpPackage`, `phpOptions`, `pools` (submodule). IMPORTANT: this module has NO `enable` option at all -- the phpfpm service is implicitly enabled via `config = mkIf (cfg.pools != { }) { ... }` rather than a declared boolean. Per the standing instruction to always watch baseline `enable` regardless, `enable` was still included in the target's watch list; oba correctly reports it as OptionNotFound on both sides (see below), which is accurate raw tool behavior, not an error.

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.enable_verdict_both_sides: OptionNotFound on both check-base.json and check-head.json (target 'phpfpm', watched_path 'enable') -- consistent with the module declaring no `enable` option; discovered_options for this module are: socket, listen, phpPackage, phpOptions, phpEnv, user, group, settings, extraConfig (x2, top-level + pool-level), phpOptions (pool-level), pools. This is why exit code is 2 (inconclusive) on all three runs rather than 0.
additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.no_asymmetric_transitions: audit-diff raw.json oba_verdict_transitions = {}, notable = [], diff.kind = 'unchanged' for the single watched identity (enable, OptionNotFound both sides). No transition of any kind, including no OBA001->PASS.
additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.reviewer_note: The actual behavioral change under audit (string-value ini escaping in toStr, exercised via phpEnv) does not correspond to any option this target's watch list covers (enable). A reviewer wanting to assess whether oba's contract-audit model has anything meaningful to say about this PR's real change would need a target watching `phpEnv` or `settings` rather than `enable` -- out of scope for this mechanical data-gathering pass, which follows the fixed watch-selection rule (baseline enable + touched option declarations only).
